calibration.reason: Clear labels and a familiar layout support the task, but misplaced focus after invalid input weakens recovery.

primary_action.expected: Select Flood and show its blue backlight on the stage.
primary_action.observed: Flood became pressed and focused; the heading and description changed to Flood and Blue backlight. Blue light outlined the performer and cast a forward shadow.

A-1440.edge_observation: Shift+Tab and Enter selected Static; the stage changed to a white beam from the left with a sharp rightward shadow. Tab moved focus to Flood while Static remained visibly filled and pressed.
A-1440.fact_check: Both cue names and descriptions match the rendered states. The image description calls the image's left side 'stage left'; theatrical stage-left orientation is not established by this illustration.
A-1440.strength: The large stage and adjacent cue details make the lighting change easy to compare.
A-1440.weakness: The long, mostly empty gap between the cue description and controls weakens their relationship.
A-1440.repair: Bring the cue controls closer to the description while retaining the large stage preview.

primary_action.expected: Select Flood and show its blue backlight on the stage.
primary_action.observed: Flood became pressed and focused; its name and Blue backlight description appeared below a blue-lit stage and forward shadow.

A-390.edge_observation: Shift+Tab and Enter selected Static. After Tab moved focus to Flood, Static remained identifiable by its filled button and heading; the white side beam and shadow were visible.
A-390.fact_check: The displayed cue names and descriptions match the observed visual changes. The stage-left terminology in the image description is not independently established.
A-390.strength: The stage, cue name, and all three controls fit together in the viewport.
A-390.weakness: The three compact buttons leave less visual breathing room around the focus outline.
A-390.repair: Increase the gap between cue buttons while keeping their labels and focus rings clear.

primary_action.expected: Select Flood and show its blue backlight on the stage.
primary_action.observed: Flood became pressed and focused, and its name and Blue backlight description appeared. The immediate capture showed the stage mid-transition; the settled blue Flood state was confirmed at 390 pixels.

B-1440.edge_observation: Shift+Tab and Enter selected Static; after Tab moved focus to Flood, Static remained filled and pressed. A settled capture showed a white beam from the right, a lit side of the figure, and a shadow extending left.
B-1440.fact_check: Static's name, description, and settled illustration agree. Flood's desktop description is present, but its settled blue appearance was not captured at this width.
B-1440.strength: The wide proscenium, restrained palette, and oversized typography create a strong theatrical composition.
B-1440.weakness: The cue label updates before the crossfade finishes, briefly pairing the new description with the previous lighting.
B-1440.repair: Shorten the crossfade or coordinate the label change with the visual transition.

primary_action.expected: Select Flood and show its blue backlight on the stage.
primary_action.observed: Flood became pressed and focused. After the transition, the stage showed blue backlight around the silhouette and a shadow toward the front.

B-390.edge_observation: Shift+Tab and Enter selected Static; Tab moved focus to Flood while the filled Static button and heading retained the selection. The settled stage showed a white beam from the right and a leftward shadow.
B-390.fact_check: The settled Flood and Static visuals support their displayed descriptions. The immediate captures show transitional mixtures rather than the final lighting states.
B-390.strength: The full-width stage and expressive typography preserve the theatrical character on a narrow screen.
B-390.weakness: The small figure makes the effect on the performer less legible than in A, and the label changes ahead of the visual transition.
B-390.repair: Make the performer larger on mobile and coordinate cue text with the crossfade.

preference.reason: Both support the keyboard flow and preserve a distinct selected state after focus moves. A makes the lighting's effect on the performer and floor easier to inspect at both widths, and its cue labels match the immediately visible state.

decision: The replacement ballot validates all four views and confirms that the selected cue remains readable after focus leaves. Both weighted scores fell to 8.45. Retain round 4, and plan a more substantial visual and layout change.
